methodologyNotes: Covers handheld/tow-behind Diver Propulsion Vehicles (DPVs) spanning pool-toy, recreational-dive, and technical-dive segments. Seed-list corrections: 'Geneinno T1 Pro' is a tethered underwater ROV/drone (six thrusters, 4K camera), not a diver propulsion vehicle, so it was replaced with the Geneinno S1 Pro, the brand's actual handheld sea scooter. 'Windek Tini' is the Sublue WhiteShark Tini sold in the US under the 'Windek' Amazon storefront name (same Chinese manufacturer, same hardware); it is listed here as sublue-whiteshark-tini with the Windek alias noted. Two products (SUEX VR Quantum, Dive Xtras BlackTip Tech) were added to represent the technical-diving segment, since a 2026 buyer researching sea scooters commonly compares consumer DPVs against professional-grade ones on price/thrust/runtime. The Sea-Doo Seascooter GTI is discontinued by BRP but is retained because it remains a widely recognized reference point in buyer comparisons and still shows up in retailer catalogs (marked accordingly). Primary manufacturer storefronts (store.sublue.com, yamahaseascooters.com, lefeet.com, asiwo.com) and several specialty retailers (wellbots.com, bhphotovideo.com, scuba.com) returned HTTP 429/403 to automated fetches during research (bot protection), so specs and prices were cross-verified instead via tradeinn.com/diveinn (an authorized EU distributor for Sublue/Yamaha/Geneinno that publishes manufacturer spec sheets, and whose product photography is used here), divers-supply.com and deep6gear.com (US authorized dive retailers), suex.it (SUEX's own site, which WAS fetchable), and press coverage (New Atlas, The Gadgeteer, PowerBoat & RIB). Where a figure could only be confirmed through live web-search retrieval of a blocked manufacturer/retailer page (rather than a direct fetch by this process), that is disclosed in the product's provenance note. priceUsd is the US starting street/list price for the base single-unit configuration (no bundles, extra batteries, or multi-pack kits) as found at the cited retailer on accessedAt; priceNote records any material spread seen across US retailers. max_speed_kmh, thrust_kgf, battery_wh and weight_kg are converted to consistent units from whatever the source published (mph, lbf, Wh/mAh+V, lb) and rounded to 1-2 significant decimals. runtime_min is the manufacturer's headline 'up to' runtime at typical/cruise settings, not the shorter continuous-max-speed runtime some DPVs also publish (noted per-product where materially different). charge_time_h and battery_wh are null for the two power-tool-battery DPVs (Dive Xtras BlackTip) because those scooters ship without a fixed battery and runtime/charge time depend entirely on which user-supplied 18V/20V power-tool battery and charger are used. A null value anywhere means the spec was not found in any source verified for this dataset, not that the feature is absent. All sources accessedAt 2026-08-01.

products.name: Sublue WhiteShark Mix
products.priceNote: US price at Divers Supply for base single-battery kit; Sublue's own US store and other retailers have listed the Mix between roughly $500-$650 depending on color and bundle.
products.provenance: Divers Supply product page (fetched 2026-08-01): 3.4 mph/5.4 kph top speed, 131 ft/40 m depth, 8.8 lbf per motor (17.6 lbf / ~8 kgf total across two motors), 30 min to 1 hour runtime depending on use, 7.7 lb/3.5 kg unit weight, ~3.5 h charge, $549.95. Battery capacity (122 Wh / 11,000 mAh Li-poly) corroborated across multiple accessory listings (muziker.com, nootica.com, B&H) for the WhiteShark Mix battery pack. Corroborated on tradeinn.com/diveinn (official EU distributor spec sheet, fetched 2026-08-01): 5.4 km/h max speed, 40 m depth, 8 kg total thrust, 3.6 kg weight (likely including battery, vs Divers Supply's 3.5 kg body-only figure) — kept the tradeinn total-weight figure. The Mix is trigger/squeeze-controlled (continuously variable thrust) rather than stepped, so speed_settings is recorded as 1. store.sublue.com returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch during research.

products.name: Sublue Navbow+
products.priceNote: US price at B&H Photo Video; US street pricing for the Navbow+ has been seen between roughly $999 and $1,079 across retailers.
products.provenance: tradeinn.com/diveinn official distributor listing (fetched 2026-08-01): 2 m/s max / 1 m/s low speed (3 gears total), 40 m depth rating, dual-motor 'quick battery change in 5 seconds', up to 60 min autonomy, listed at €1,920.99 (not used as priceUsd — see B&H figure). store.sublue.com's own Navbow+ page (store.sublue.com/products/navbow-plus) returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch, so thrust (15 kgf), battery (158 Wh Li-ion, ~1,100 g cell + ~3,400 g body), weight (4.5 kg total) and charge time (~3.5 h) were compiled from live web-search retrieval of that same official page together with matching figures on wellbots.com and Amazon US Navbow+ listings — all three sources independently agreed on 158 Wh and 15 kgf. Runtime breakdown per official spec: ~45 min continuous in Free mode, ~20 min in Sport mode, ~8-17 min in Turbo mode; 60 min is the manufacturer's blended 'up to' figure for mixed/intermittent use. Buoyancy characteristic not stated in any source checked, left null rather than guessed. US price of $999 is a B&H Photo Video listing found via search; B&H's own product page (bhphotovideo.com) returned HTTP 429/403 to direct fetch.

products.name: Sublue WhiteShark Tini
products.priceNote: US price as sold on Amazon under the 'Windek' storefront name (same Sublue-manufactured hardware); Sublue's own global listings and diveinn.com price the Tini differently by region.
products.provenance: This is the same product listed under seed name 'Windek Tini': Windek is the brand name Sublue's Tini/Navbow line is sold under on Amazon US (confirmed via matching Amazon listings for 'WINDEK Tini' and 'sublue Tini' showing identical specs/photos), not a separate manufacturer. Specs sourced from tradeinn.com/diveinn official distributor spec table (fetched 2026-08-01): high/low speed 1.4/1.1 m/s, 20 m max depth, 98 Wh battery (870 g cell), 3 kg total weight, 2 h charge time, 40 min power-system runtime (150 min for the handle/remote alone), two-level speed switch. Some third-party US retail listings advertise '131 ft / 40 m' depth for the Tini, which appears to conflate it with the Navbow+'s depth rating; the tradeinn official spec table's 20 m figure was preferred as the more detailed, manufacturer-sourced number. Thrust and buoyancy were not stated in any source checked and are left null. store.sublue.com/products/tini returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch; the $429 US price comes from a live web-search read of the Amazon 'Windek'-branded listing.

products.name: Yamaha Seascooter RDS300
products.priceNote: US price at Divers Supply; West Marine has listed the RDS300 at $899.99.
products.provenance: Divers Supply (fetched 2026-08-01): 3 mph/4.8 km/h top speed, 100 ft/30 m depth, 18 lb/8.2 kg including battery, up to 1.5 h (90 min) runtime, sealed lead-acid battery, $695. Corroborated on tradeinn.com/diveinn (fetched 2026-08-01): identical speed/depth/runtime/weight figures. Battery capacity (12 V, 12 Ah = 144 Wh) and 6-8 h recharge time from Yamaha OEM replacement-battery listings (B&H, yamahaseascooters.com battery page, Raion Group) — used the 7 h midpoint of the stated 6-8 h range. US model has 2-level rotational speed control; the EU version of the RDS300 ships with single-speed control only. yamahaseascooters.com returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch.

products.name: Yamaha Seascooter 500Li
products.priceNote: US price at Divers Supply for the flagship 500Li configuration.
products.provenance: Divers Supply (fetched 2026-08-01): $1,595 price; battery capacity not listed on that page. Corroborated on tradeinn.com/diveinn (fetched 2026-08-01) and manufacturer marketing copy repeated across retailers: 500 W motor, 4.35 mph/7 km/h top speed, 130 ft/40 m depth, 3-level speed control, up to 90 min runtime, 21 lb/9.5 kg including battery, superior flood prevention and automatic buoyancy adjustment. Battery is a 22.2 V 12 Ah lithium-ion pack (22.2 x 12 = 266.4 Wh) per Yamaha OEM replacement-battery listings (LeisurePro, Scuba.com); charge time 7-9 h per the same listings, 8 h midpoint used. yamahaseascooters.com and westmarine.com returned HTTP 429/errors to direct fetch.

products.name: Geneinno S2
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP, positioned below the original Geneinno S1 ($689).

specs.buoyancy: Slightly positive (floats to surface if released)

products.provenance: New Atlas article (published 2020-04-01, fetched 2026-08-01): 3.2/4.3 km/h two-speed dual 350 W motors, 10 kg/22 lb combined thrust, 30 m/98 ft max depth, 97 Wh battery (under the 100 Wh airline limit) giving 45 min runtime, 2.7 kg/5.9 lb weight, $399, GoPro-compatible mount, iOS/Android app monitoring. Charge time (1.5 h) confirmed separately via Geneinno S2 user-manual/FCC filing and multiple retailer listings. Corroborated on tradeinn.com/diveinn (fetched 2026-08-01), which lists an ultra-portable dual-thruster DPV with two-speed control and airline-approved battery matching this description, though that page did not itself restate every numeric spec.

products.name: Geneinno S1 Pro
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP per Geneinno-focused press coverage (DeeperBlue.com / The Scuba News); a UK distributor (powerboatandrib.com, cited as this product's source) sells the same unit for £565 plus shipping.
products.provenance: Seed list said 'Geneinno T1 Pro' — that name actually belongs to a tethered underwater ROV/camera drone (6 thrusters, 4K/30fps camera, 574 ft depth rating, sold as a photography tool, not a diver propulsion vehicle). Substituted the brand's actual handheld sea scooter, the S1 Pro. Specs from powerboatandrib.com (fetched 2026-08-01): two wing-mounted enclosed-propeller motors giving 26 lbs/12 kg thrust, 4 mph/6.4 km/h top speed (2.2 mph/3.5 km/h low), 164 ft/50 m max depth, 6,300 mAh Li-polymer battery swappable in 10 seconds, ~1 h run time at full depth (45 min figure used here matches the more commonly repeated Amazon/manufacturer spec of '45 mins running time'; provenance discrepancy noted), 3.7 kg weight, ~1.5 h charge, 1,000+ hour motor lifespan, 365-day warranty. Battery Wh not stated by any source checked (only mAh, with pack voltage not confirmed) so left null rather than computed from an assumed voltage. Buoyancy not stated, left null. lefeet.com/geneinno retailer pages (gearsjoy.com, maxstrata.com) and deeperblue.com returned HTTP 429/403 to direct fetch; the $689 figure was read via live web search of deeperblue.com/thescubanews.com rather than a direct fetch of those pages.

products.name: Asiwo Mako (Electric Kickboard)
products.priceNote: Regular price at asiwo.com; frequently discounted to $269.
products.provenance: Asiwo markets this single product as both the 'Mako' underwater scooter and the 'Mako Electric Kickboard' (a swim-kickboard-shaped handheld DPV aimed at pools/snorkeling/nearshore use rather than deep diving — Asiwo explicitly says it should not be used as a deep-diving scooter, so no max depth is published and max_depth_m is left null). asiwo.com returned HTTP 429 to every direct fetch attempted; specs were compiled from two independent live web-search reads of the official product page that agreed on the same figures: 36 V/300 W motor, three speeds (5 ft/s, 3.3 ft/s, 2 ft/s = 1.5/1.0/0.6 m/s for adults/general use/children), up to 8 kg thrust, up to 60 min runtime, 3-4 h recharge (3.5 h midpoint used), detachable airline-compliant 37V/2.5A/92.5 Wh battery, ~5.7 lb/2.6 kg weight, $299 regular / $269 sale price. Given the lower confidence from not being able to directly fetch the manufacturer page, no image is included per the 'omit rather than guess' rule — no independently confirmed direct image file URL for this specific model was found.

products.name: Lefeet S1 Pro
products.priceNote: US list price at Divers Supply (listed sold out at time of access); other US retailers have shown sale prices as low as $699.

specs.buoyancy: Slightly negative; neutral achievable with optional S1 Pro Buoyancy Float accessory

products.provenance: Divers Supply spec table (fetched 2026-08-01): 40 m max depth, 8 kg/18 lbs thrust, three speeds (low/med/high, top speed 1.8 m/s = 6.5 km/h), 45-70 min main-unit runtime (70 min upper bound used, achieved at lowest speed setting), 4,400 mAh/25.2 V/97.68 Wh battery with 2.5 h charge time, 5.51 lb/2.5 kg weight including battery, remote control good for ~2.5 h separately, $799 (marked sold out at access time). Buoyancy detail (slightly negative, Buoyancy Float accessory sold separately for neutral trim) from Lefeet's own accessory product naming, corroborated across multiple retailer listings. lefeet.com, wellbots.com, and B&H Photo Video (bhphotovideo.com) returned HTTP 429/403 to direct fetch.

products.name: Lefeet C1 (Seagull C1)
products.priceNote: US regular price; discounted to $375.20 during Amazon Prime Day 2026.

specs.buoyancy: Slightly positive (floats to surface if released)

products.provenance: The Gadgeteer (fetched 2026-08-01, current retail unit): 8 kgf dual-motor thrust, 97.2 Wh TSA-compliant swappable battery, 6.6 lb/3 kg weight, up to 60 min runtime, $469 regular price ($375.20 Prime Day 2026). Depth (30 m/98 ft), top speed (1.6 m/s = 5.8 km/h, with a lower 1.3 m/s gear), and 2-hour-charge-for-25-to-45-minutes-of-use figures corroborated on New Atlas, whose C1 coverage (published 2021-04-29, fetched 2026-08-01) describes an earlier Indiegogo-crowdfunded version of the C1 concept with matching depth/speed but 200 W-rated motors and Indiegogo pricing ($299-$459); Lefeet appears to have carried the 'C1'/'Seagull C1' name forward from that 2021 campaign to the refined product now sold at retail (first widely available per retail listings around March 2025), so releaseDate reflects the current retail SKU, not the 2021 crowdfunding date. lefeet.com and wellbots.com returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch.

products.name: Sea-Doo Seascooter GTI
products.priceNote: Last known US list price at Divers Supply (listed sold out at access time); this model is discontinued by BRP and included as a widely recognized reference point still seen in buyer comparisons and residual retailer/used stock.
products.provenance: Divers Supply (fetched 2026-08-01, listed sold out): 2.5 mph/4 km/h single-speed propulsion, 18 lb/8.2 kg including battery, up to 2 h runtime, $449.99. Depth rating (tested to 115 ft/35 m, rated to 100 ft/30 m) and 12 V/14 Ah battery (168 Wh) from other retailer listings for the same SKU (Overtons, Scooter Motion, direct fetch not obtained for these — read via search). Not to be confused with BRP's current 'Sea-Doo GTI' personal watercraft (jet ski) product line, which is an entirely different, much larger vehicle; this is the small handheld dive/snorkel scooter BRP sold under license years ago and has since discontinued. Thrust figure and exact charge time not found in any source checked and left null.

products.name: SUEX VR Quantum
products.priceNote: US technical-dive retail price (paragondivestore.com); SUEX's own Italian site lists €3,200 and a UK distributor (dirdirect.com) lists £3,340 — the difference reflects US import/distribution markup typical for this category, not a different configuration.

specs.buoyancy: Neutral trim via adjustable water ballast system

products.provenance: SUEX's own product page (suex.it, fetched 2026-08-01 — one of the few manufacturer sites in this dataset not bot-blocked): 70 m/min (4.2 km/h) max speed, 90 min runtime at max speed / 220 min at 45 m/min cruise, 100 m/328 ft max depth, 220 N static thrust (220/9.80665 = 22.4 kgf), 587.7 Wh Li-ion battery (25.2 V nominal), 8.5 kg without battery / 11.7 kg with battery, 8-level speed regulator with SPORT/ECO modes, neutral trim via adjustable water ballast, Bluetooth connectivity, listed at €3,200. Diveavenue.com (fetched 2026-08-01) confirms SUEX VR-series DPVs are sold through independent European dive retailers, corroborating the product's existence and category, though its page covers the VR series generically rather than restating Quantum-specific numbers. US price ($5,530) read via live web search of paragondivestore.com rather than a direct fetch (paragondivestore.com and dirdirect.com both returned HTTP 429 to direct fetch attempts). No image included: the only product photo found on a fetchable page (diveavenue.com) is captioned generically as 'SUEX DPV VR Series' and could not be confirmed to specifically depict the Quantum variant rather than the VR-X/VR Nemo/Voyager siblings in the same body shell, so it was omitted rather than risk mismatching the wrong model's photo to this listing.

products.name: Dive Xtras BlackTip Tech
products.priceNote: US price at Deep6Gear for the Tech-trim scooter body only; power-tool batteries and charger are sold separately and not included.

specs.buoyancy: Nose runs slightly positive vs. tail; neutral trim achievable with battery/weight combination

products.provenance: Deep6Gear (fetched 2026-08-01): 24 lb/10.9 kg, 24 in/61 cm long, 330 ft/100 m depth rating, 150 ft/min (45 m/min = 2.7 km/h) cruise speed, 210 ft/min (64 m/min = 3.84 km/h) continuous max speed, 238 ft/min (73 m/min = 4.35 km/h) boost-mode max speed (used here as max_speed_kmh, consistent with how other scooters' short-burst 'turbo/boost' top speed is used elsewhere in this dataset), 57 lb/25.9 kg boost-mode max thrust, runtime at cruise speed of 50 min on a 5 Ah power-tool battery or 123 min on a 12 Ah battery (123 min used as the manufacturer's spec'd maximum), boost-mode runtime only 7 min, eight speed modes, $2,099, currently on backorder (~3-week wait) at time of access. The BlackTip has no fixed internal battery — it runs on user-supplied 18V/20V DCB-format power-tool batteries (5/6/9/12 Ah) — so battery_wh and charge_time_h are genuinely unfixed and left null rather than assigned an assumed pack size. Buoyancy detail from the same page: nose floats slightly positive relative to the tail; a neutral trim is achievable by combining specific battery/weight choices. dive-xtras.com and divegearexpress.com returned HTTP 429/403 to direct fetch.
